subject.title: fix: tighten control ui input validation [AI]

question: Should config.patch silently reject __defineGetter__, __defineSetter__, __lookupGetter__, and __lookupSetter__ even though the shared pollution guard treats them as ordinary keys?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility-versus-defense-in-depth choice: source review can establish the behavior change, but cannot decide whether OpenClaw wants to invalidate those record-key names without maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve the existing key contract
options.body: Remove the four-name merge-patch denylist and merge the independently justified Control UI URL and filename hardening.

options.title: Adopt the narrower patch contract
options.body: Keep the denylist, explicitly approve the silent compatibility change, and add upgrade-focused coverage for affected schema-owned record maps.

recommendation.title: Preserve the existing key contract
recommendation.body: Remove the four-name merge-patch denylist and merge the independently justified Control UI URL and filename hardening.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of the Control UI and gateway boundary where most of this PR lands.
